clue.text: Livelier Master of Ceremonies cooked the pasta

indicators.note: cooked suggests something worked over and changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A livelier host at a party prepares the pasta course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' tells you to rearrange the letters of LIVELIER together with MC.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermicelli is a very thin Italian noodle, a kind of pasta.

clue.text: To create artwork, and so on is hard

parts.note: etc. (et cetera) means and so on
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Making art, along with other things, is a difficult business.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to make a picture by cutting lines into a metal plate with acid, an artistic print process.

clue.text: Lament got confused in one's mind

indicators.note: got confused says the letters of the word lament are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A sad song becomes muddled inside someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got confused' tells you to rearrange the six letters of LAMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental describes what happens in the head, inside a person's thoughts.

clue.text: Roman assemblies that US spy organisation is about to leave out

indicators.note: is about means the spy agency's letters surround the next piece

parts.note: the CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency, the US spy organisation
to omit something is to leave it out

explanation.surface: Ancient Roman gatherings that the American intelligence agency is about to exclude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' reads as 'is going to', but it is the container signal. The comitia were the voting assemblies of the Roman people.
explanation.definitionFit: The comitia were the popular voting gatherings of ancient Rome, a historical term.

clue.text: Spike to weave around

explanation.surface: Doctoring something, then winding threads round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spike a drink is to add alcohol or a drug to it, and to thread a cord in and out of eyelets is the other sense.

clue.text: Unwell Frenchman's here first thing, it's illegal!

parts.note: ill means unwell
ici is the French word for here

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word thing is used

explanation.surface: A sick French visitor exclaims that something is against the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frenchman's here' asks for the French word for 'here', ICI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illicit is forbidden by law, a close synonym of unlawful.

clue.text: Dish unable to hold this food

annotationWithheld.why: Dish unable to hold this food (6,4): DISH UNABLE gives the letters of the cheese, but no word in the clue as held signals an anagram, and the scan is not available to check for a missing word
annotationWithheld.clue: Dish unable to hold this food

clue.text: Raises weapons in holders to cover chair perhaps

parts.note: to up something is to raise it
holsters are the holders a gun or other weapon is kept in

explanation.surface: Someone lifts guns into their cases in order to protect a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raises' gives UP in its verb sense (to up a price is to raise it).
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster is to fit padding, springs and fabric onto furniture; a chair is one example of what gets this treatment.

clue.text: Discourage many a politician

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number, so many
MP is a Member of Parliament, a British politician

explanation.surface: Lots of people try to put off a member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' gives D, the Roman numeral 500, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To damp enthusiasm is to dampen or deaden it, which is what discouraging does.

clue.text: A cost effective way to make the cinema cool?

indicators.note: a way to make something from these words means rearranging their letters into it

explanation.surface: Air-conditioning a picture house on a tight budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way to make' tells you to rearrange the letters of CINEMA and COOL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Economical means thrifty, giving good value for the money spent.

clue.text: In the excavation nothing blue was discovered

parts.note: a dig is an archaeological excavation
O looks like zero, so it stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An archaeological team finds only empty ground, apart from something blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep shade of blue, between blue and violet in the rainbow.

clue.text: Gail and May both suffered from cramp

indicators.note: suffered from suggests the two names are knocked about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two women both had a muscle spasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffered from' tells you to rearrange the letters of GAIL and MAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Myalgia is the medical term for muscle pain, which a cramp is.

clue.text: Strong magnifier shows precosmic stew contains nothing

indicators.note: contains means the mixed letters hold the next piece inside them
a stew is a jumble cooked together, so the letters of precosmic are mixed up

parts.note: O looks like zero, so it stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An instrument reveals that a soup from before the universe began is empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' tells you to rearrange PRECOSMIC, and 'contains' puts O inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A microscope is a lab instrument that enlarges tiny objects many times.

clue.text: Reply of sailor to the French seems responsible

parts.note: an answer is a reply
AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
le is the French word for the

explanation.surface: A seaman's response in French appears to be accountable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being answerable means being accountable, required to explain your actions.

clue.text: Quick drink around teatime

indicators.note: around means the drink's letters wrap round the next piece

parts.note: ale is a type of beer, a drink
IV is the Roman numeral four, and four o'clock is traditional British teatime

explanation.surface: A fast pint taken in the late afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' here is the old sense, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in its old sense means living, as in the phrase about the quick and the dead.

clue.text: Gets tight with thieves!

explanation.surface: Something squeezes in, alongside some robbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe that pinches grips the foot too closely, and to thieve is to steal, slang 'pinch'.

clue.text: Master returns in the afternoon with something for lab

indicators.note: in means the reversed title goes inside the next piece

parts.note: PM (post meridiem) means the afternoon

indicators.note: returns means the word for master is read backwards

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a master

explanation.surface: A teacher comes back after lunch with laboratory equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses the title, and 'in' places it inside the afternoon abbreviation; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A prism is a block of glass used in physics labs to split light into a spectrum.

clue.text: Watchful for signal of attack

explanation.surface: On guard for the warning of a raid.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert person is wide awake and vigilant, and an air-raid warning siren is also called this.

clue.text: Found on stage

explanation.surface: Discovered in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To found metal is to cast it in a mould, and the actors appearing in a play make up the company list.

clue.text: Miss French?

parts.note: a miss is a girl, and the clue asks for the French word for 'she', a magazine title too

explanation.definitionFit: Elle is the French pronoun for a female person, as a miss is.

clue.text: A very big noise in the navy

parts.note: vast means very big

explanation.surface: A huge racket aboard a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sailor's call: the cry used at sea to order a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is the nautical command meaning stop or hold, shouted aboard ship.

clue.text: Surprisingly eager to fall in with the plans

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the letters of eager come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone unexpectedly keen to go along with the arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' tells you to rearrange EAGER; TO is kept as written. 'the plans' is the object of the phrase, not part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall in with a scheme is to accept or consent to it.

clue.text: Board with gold picture was vivid

parts.note: a table is a board, as in bed and board
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A table with gilding made a striking image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was vivid' hints at tableau vivant, a living picture staged by actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene, especially a group of motionless figures arranged as an image.

clue.text: Moved without the extremes of anger because of being too old

indicators.note: without the extremes means the first and last letters of the word moved are dropped

parts.note: rage means anger

explanation.surface: Someone stirred, angry because of their age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without the extremes' strips M and D from MOVED to leave OVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overage means beyond the permitted age limit.

clue.text: It's insanity to crowd around the back end

indicators.note: around means the crowd's letters wrap round the next piece

parts.note: a mass is a crowd

indicators.note: back means the word end is read backwards

explanation.surface: It is crazy to throng about the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word end, and 'around' wraps the crowd round it; 'the back end' reads as a rear but splits into indicator and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness is a synonym of lunacy, a state of being out of one's mind.

clue.text: Left wing fellow returns showing agreement

indicators.note: returns means the joined words are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: red is the political colour of the left
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: A socialist academic comes back and agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses REDDON as a whole. A don is a university teacher, often a college fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A nodder is a person who bobs their head in assent, signalling yes.

clue.text: Small coins to dangle in church

indicators.note: in means the word for dangle goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to hang is to dangle

explanation.surface: Loose coins swing in a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Change is the loose coins in your pocket.

clue.text: It's a mixture of wine

indicators.note: mixture of means the letters of the words its and a are jumbled

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters ITS

explanation.surface: A blended wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture of' tells you to rearrange ITS and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: It might make a perch

parts.note: a perch is a bird's resting place, but also an old unit of length of five and a half yards, which has another name

explanation.definitionFit: A long rod can serve as a bird's roost, and in old measures a rod, perch and pole are the same length.

clue.text: Eddie performed 500 soft pieces at the music festival

indicators.note: performed suggests the letters are put through their paces into a new order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Eddie played many gentle pieces at a Welsh singing contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' tells you to rearrange EDDIE, D and SOFT; 'pieces' adds to the picture. An eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of music and poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: An eisteddfod is a Welsh competitive gathering of singers, musicians and poets.

clue.text: Not much colour-have a quiet drink!

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
ale is a type of beer, a drink

explanation.surface: Looking washed out, so take a gentle pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale means light in shade, lacking strong colour.

clue.text: Late notices?

parts.note: late can mean recently dead, so these are newspaper announcements about people who have died, not reminders sent overdue

explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers print death announcements with accounts of the lives of the deceased.
